matching: A must_produce entry is matched by exactly one comment in the output's comment set at one of the entry's locations, carrying every reviewer the entry lists in its category tag, a tier from the entry's tiers list, and content the entry's detail describes. A must_not entry is violated by any output the entry's detail forbids. A log_requirement is met by an adjudication-log entry whose content the requirement describes. An allowed_extras entry excuses a comment only when the comment is at one of the entry's locations AND says what the entry's detail describes; any other comment matching no must_produce entry counts against precision. report_requirements must all hold.
report_requirements: The output contains, in order: a review body, a numbered comment set, and an adjudication log.
The review body contains an attribution line naming the criteria the review was generated from.
Every comment in the comment set begins with a [category][tier] prefix whose tier is blocking or follow-up.
The comment set is ordered most severe first, and its first comment is the starvation defect (must_produce id starvation).

must_produce.detail: the unconditional advance of lastRefillNanos on line 41 starves any caller polling faster than once per second after the initial burst, silently and permanently, contradicting the documented refill contract; the comment states the mechanism and a fix confined to the refill logic

one comment, not two, for the documented thread-safety claim over unsynchronized mutable state, crediting both arch-review and testing-review; it demands either real synchronization plus an attacking test or deletion of the claim

one comment for the never-throws-and-clamps sentence contradicted by the constructor's IllegalArgumentException and by refillPerSecond being unvalidated; the ruling is either fix-the-code-to-clamp or fix-the-doc-to-state-the-throw, and the adjudication log carries both positions
the javadoc example calls acquirePermit(), a method that does not exist; the fix names tryAcquire()
the clock-seam/strategy decomposition demand survives as follow-up, never blocking; it may carry a smallest-step note but must not be dropped
the field-grouping readability nit survives as follow-up
the paragraph-ordering nit (guarantees before mechanics) survives as follow-up, either as its own comment or folded into a comment at overlapping lines with writing-review credited

must_not.detail: no comment derives from the zero-capacity finding (testing report T3): its quoted line 30 is the constructor throw, not a return, and a zero-capacity limiter cannot be constructed because the constructor throws first; posting it in any form violates this entry
no blocking comment demands the decomposition/restructuring of the class; a blocking tier on the clock-seam/strategy demand violates this entry
neither the field-grouping nit nor the paragraph-ordering nit carries a blocking tier
no input finding is absent from both the comment set and the adjudication log

log_requirements: The zero-capacity finding (testing report T3) appears as returned, with the verification failure stated: the quote does not match line 30 and/or the claim is impossible because the constructor throws for capacity <= 0.

The no-throw disagreement appears with both positions stated (arch-review: make the code honor the documented clamping; writing-review: correct the document to state the throw) and a deciding reason for the ruling.
The thread-safety merge appears, naming both source findings.
The posture facts used in tiering are stated: no callers outside tests, and the limiter.enabled flag defaulting to false.

allowed_extras.detail: a separate comment isolating the unvalidated refillPerSecond half of the no-throw finding (a zero or negative rate is accepted and never refills), instead of folding it into the no-throw comment
a note in the review body naming dimensions no input report covered (for example performance or security), presented as unreviewed rather than as findings
